translation: 我们研究了具有固定、已知有向反馈图的对抗性多臂老虎机的的一阶遗憾保证。对于强可观测图，[ACBDK15] 建立了 $\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{αT})$ 的极小极大遗憾，其中 $α$ 表示图的独立数，$T$ 表示时间范围。另一方面，现有的最佳一阶界为 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{(κ+1) L^\star})$ [LLZ20]，其中 $κ$ 表示满足 $κ+1\geqα$ 的团划分数，$L^\star$ 表示最优臂的累积损失，这导致最坏情况与一阶保证中的图依赖性之间存在差距。在本文中，我们通过获得 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ 的期望遗憾界弥补了这一差距。我们的第一个结果是针对自感知图（其中每个顶点都有一个自循环）的特殊情况的算法。该算法将 EXP3 [ACBFS02] 的更新与受通过优化进行探索 [LS20] 启发的采样规则相结合。更具体地说，我们构造了一个映射，其不动点产生的采样分布可以根据学习者的损失和图的独立数来控制单轮遗憾余项，这对于推导最优一阶保证至关重要。我们进一步证明了可以通过几何收敛迭代在多项式时间内计算出足够精确的不动点。最后，通过采用 [LLZ20] 的两层聚合方法，我们将该算法推广到一般的强可观测图，并实现了相同的 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ 保证。
tldr: 本文解决了对抗性反馈图老虎机中一阶遗憾界的图依赖差距，提出了达到 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ 遗憾界的新算法。
ai_comments: 该论文在带反馈图的对抗性多臂老鼠问题中，首次给出了关于图独立数 α 和最优臂累积损失 L* 的近最优一阶遗憾界，弥补了最坏情况与一阶遗憾界之间的图依赖差距，技术上结合了EXP3更新与基于优化的探索采样规则。
motivation: 现有的对抗性带反馈图老虎机的最坏情况遗憾界与一阶遗憾界在图的依赖性上存在差距（最坏情况依赖独立数 α，而现有的一阶界依赖团划分数 κ+1），本文旨在弥补这一理论差距。
method: 提出了一种结合EXP3更新和受“通过优化进行探索”启发的新型采样规则的算法。通过构造固定点映射来控制单轮遗憾余项，并利用两层聚合方法将其扩展到一般强可观测图。
results: 对于强可观测的反馈图，本文算法取得了期望遗憾界为 $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ 的近最优一阶遗憾保证。
conclusion: 本文成功将反馈图中独立数 α 的最坏情况依赖推广到一阶遗憾界中，提出了针对自感知图及一般强可观测图的近最优算法。

title: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models
authors: Fengji Jing, Guy Laban
abstract: Voice-interactive large language models process both what a speaker says and how they say it, yet the two channels do not always agree. We ask whether that disagreement degrades speech emotion recognition. Mapping text and audio into a shared valence-arousal-dominance space, we convert the distance between them into a continuous, threshold-free incongruence score with a two-component Gaussian mixture, and validate the score against human judgement. We evaluate three audiocapable models on acted, conversational and spontaneous speech (eNTERFACE'05, MELD and CMU-MOSEI). With the model held constant across modalities, incongruence raises the odds of error whenever audio is present, in every corpus, after controlling for the ground-truth emotion and for distance in the feature space. Supervised classifiers trained on the same features behave in the opposite way, which suggests that the difficulty lies in how these models combine raw evidence rather than in the signal itself. Text-only effects are unreliable: swapping only the model that reads the transcript reverses their sign on one corpus. Rebuilding the score without the emotion lexicon reproduces the central result, and among six simpler alternatives it is the only label-free score that predicts error in all three corpora. Code, data tables and prompts are released.

title: Dynamic Persuasion: Managing Reputation under Censored Feedback
authors: Ahmet E. Arcaklioglu, Ceyhun Eksin
abstract: We study a long-run sender who repeatedly communicates about a state to a sequence of myopic receivers and whose credibility is a public score updated from past interactions. Receivers face a lemon loss and an opportunity loss, and their behavior depends on these only through a single index, the tolerance. Because the score records only detected misrepresentations, it rests above the sender's true honesty rate; we characterize this credibility premium in closed form. In a fluid limit in which the score adjusts slowly, no policy earns more than operating at a single credibility level, and the sender's gain from managing credibility equals the value of the premium: against receivers who correct for imperfect detection, that gain vanishes. At a fixed adjustment speed, every policy is bounded by the fluid value plus a term linear in the speed. We then study three policy classes, linear, (s,S), and threshold, obtain the optimal parameters of the linear and threshold classes in closed form, show how receiver losses shape them, and show that, under an approximation, the optimal (s,S) band collapses to a threshold. Simulations of the dynamics agree with the closed forms and indicate where the single-level conclusion stops: bands pay when switching modes is costly, and cycles pay when demand is seasonal.
comment: 44 pages, 8 figures. A preliminary version of part of this work appears in Proc. IEEE CDC 2026
zh_title: 动态说服：在审查反馈下管理声誉
translation: 我们研究了一个长期发送者，他反复地就一个状态与一系列短期的接收者沟通，并且他的信誉是一个从过去互动中更新的公开分数。接收者面临柠檬损失和机会损失，他们的行为仅通过一个单一指标——容忍度——来决定。因为分数只记录了被发现的虚假陈述，所以它高于发送者真实的诚实率；我们以封闭形式表征了这种信誉溢价。在分数调整缓慢的流体极限下，没有策略能获得超过在单一信誉水平下运作的收益，而发送者通过管理信誉获得的收益等于溢价的价值：对于那些纠正了不完美检测的接收者，这种收益消失了。在固定的调整速度下，每个策略的收益都受到流体价值加上一个与速度成线性关系的项的限制。然后我们研究了三种策略类别：线性、(s,S)和阈值，以封闭形式得到了线性和阈值类别的最优参数，展示了接收者损失如何影响它们，并表明在近似下，最优的(s,S)区间会缩减为一个阈值。动态模拟与封闭形式一致，并指出了单一水平结论失效的地方：当转换模式成本高昂时，区间策略（bands）有优势，而当需求有季节性时，周期策略（cycles）有优势。
tldr: 该研究探讨了一个长期发送者如何通过管理其声誉（一个公开的、根据过去互动更新的评分）来与一系列短期接收者沟通。接收者会根据柠檬损失和机会损失来决定行为，而发送者的声誉评分会高于其真实诚实率，因为评分只记录了被发现的虚假陈述。研究发现，在评分调整缓慢的情况下，单一的信誉水平最优，并且发送者通过管理信誉获得的收益等于信誉溢价的价值。在固定的调整速度下，任何策略的收益都受到该速度线性影响的限制。研究还分析了三种策略（线性、(s,S)和阈值），并得到了线性策略和阈值策略的最优参数。模拟结果表明，当转换模式成本高昂时，区间策略（bands）有优势，而当需求有季节性时，周期策略（cycles）有优势。
ai_comments: 该研究在理论上为理解动态环境下的声誉管理和信息传播提供了一个严谨的框架。通过区分发送者的长期性和接收者的短期性，以及考虑审查反馈的现实情况，模型具有一定的现实意义。然而，模型假设接收者是“短视的”（myopic），这可能限制了其在某些复杂博弈场景下的适用性。此外，“流体极限”和“近似”等分析方法虽然简化了问题，但也可能忽略一些重要的离散动态或非线性效应。未来的研究可以考虑引入更复杂的接收者行为，或者探索更精确的数值方法来处理动态博弈。
motivation: 研究动机在于理解一个长期发送者如何在与一系列短期接收者进行沟通时管理其声誉（公开评分），以及这种声誉管理如何影响其收益，特别是当反馈信息（评分）可能存在审查（仅记录被发现的虚假陈述）的情况下。
method: 该研究通过建立一个模型来分析发送者与接收者的互动。模型考虑了发送者的长期性和接收者的短期性，以及一个公开的、基于过去互动的声誉评分。研究中采用了流体极限（fluid limit）的方法来分析评分调整缓慢的情况，并在此基础上推导了最优策略。此外，研究还分析了三种具体的策略类别：线性策略、(s,S)策略和阈值策略，并得到了其中两种策略的最优参数。通过模拟来验证理论结果并探索其适用范围。
results: 研究结果表明，在评分调整缓慢的情况下，发送者应该维持单一的信誉水平以最大化收益，此时发送者通过管理信誉获得的收益等于信誉溢价的价值。在固定的评分调整速度下，任何策略的收益都受到该速度线性影响的限制。研究还确定了线性策略和阈值策略的最优参数，并指出接收者的损失会影响这些策略。模拟结果显示，当转换模式的成本较高时，区间策略（bands）比单一信誉水平更优；当需求具有季节性时，周期策略（cycles）则更有效。
conclusion: 该研究得出了几个关键结论：1. 在评分调整缓慢的理想情况下，单一信誉水平是最优的。2. 发送者通过管理信誉获得的收益与信誉溢价的价值相等，并且在接收者能完全纠正不完美检测的情况下，这种收益会消失。3. 评分的调整速度对策略的收益有线性影响。4. 实际应用中，区间策略和周期策略在特定条件下（如模式转换成本高或需求季节性）可能优于单一信誉水平。

title: An Empirical Study of Gas Optimization Practices in Solidity Smart Contracts
authors: Francesco Salzano, Paolo Martino, Simone Scalabrino, Rocco Oliveto, Remo Pareschi
abstract: In the Ethereum ecosystem, smart contract execution is governed by a gas model where every computational operation incurs a direct economic cost. Consequently, gas efficiency is a critical requirement for the economic sustainability and widespread adoption of decentralized applications. Despite the importance of cost-effective development, there remains a significant gap between theoretical optimization patterns and the actual practices applied by developers in real-world projects. This paper presents an empirical study investigating gas optimization practices in open-source Solidity repositories created on GitHub between 2018 and 2025. Adopting a Mining Software Repositories approach, we analyzed a dataset of gas-related commits identified through a multi-stage pipeline involving NLP-based filtering and manual qualitative inspection. Based on the analysis of 400 representative commits, we derive an empirical taxonomy of gas optimization strategies consisting of 8 macro-categories and 36 subcategories. Our findings reveal that optimization efforts span multiple levels of abstraction, from low-level arithmetic refinements and bytecode-size reductions to broader architectural changes such as logic internalization and external call reduction. Furthermore, we observe that developers often manage complex trade-offs between execution frequency, safety checks, and computational costs, highlighting that effective optimization is inherently context-dependent. This study provides a practical knowledge base for the design of future developer support tools and advances the understanding of cost-aware software engineering in the blockchain domain.

title: TensorSSM: Memorizing Spatial Position in Dynamic State Space for Tensor Core Generation
authors: Sheng Zhang, Xinyi Wang, Maolin Wang, Xiangyu Zhao
abstract: High-dimensional tensors are ubiquitous in real-world applications but lead to massive storage overhead. Functional tensor decomposition addresses this by employing neural networks to map element coordinates to tensor cores, significantly reducing the parameters for data compression. However, existing functional methods typically flatten high-order tensors into 1D sequences. This folding operation causes highly overlapping local coordinate sequences and struggles to capture complex cross-mode spatial dependencies, severely limiting their expressiveness on diverse datasets. To tackle these challenges, we propose TensorSSM, a novel Implicit Neural Representation (INR) for functional decomposition method that memorizes spatial positions within a dynamic State Space Model (SSM). Specifically, TensorSSM first decomposes mode-wise coordinates into sequences spit by K-ary rule, encoding spatial tokens from coarse to fine, which effectively captures spatial variations. Furthermore, we extend the SSM's state space to explicitly map cross-mode spatial dependencies, allowing inter-mode interactions to enhance the updates of each mode. By integrating cross-mode information from previous hidden states into the current state transitions, TensorSSM effectively expands tensor representation along two dimensions: the sequence dimension for coarse-to-fine spatial tokens, and the state dimension for cross-mode memorization. This design effectively integrates spatial information into the state space and the tensor core, substantially advancing the state adaptability and enhancing the expressiveness of the data compression. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TensorSSM achieves significantly high reconstruction accuracy and storage efficiency, exhibiting robust expressiveness across diverse tensor datasets without relying on strict spatial assumptions.
zh_title: TensorSSM：动态状态空间中用于张量核心生成的空间位置记忆方法
translation: 高维张量在现实世界应用中无处不在，但会导致巨大的存储开销。功能性张量分解通过采用神经网络将元素坐标映射到张量核心来解决这一问题，从而显著减少了用于数据压缩的参数。然而，现有的功能性方法通常将高阶张量展平为1D序列。这种折叠操作会导致高度重叠的局部坐标序列，并且难以捕捉复杂的跨模态空间依赖关系，从而严重限制了它们在多样化数据集上的表现力。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了TensorSSM，这是一种用于功能分解的新型隐式神经表示（INR）方法，它在动态状态空间模型（SSM）中记忆空间位置。具体而言，TensorSSM首先通过K-ary规则将按模式的坐标分解为序列，从粗到细编码空间标记，这有效地捕捉了空间变化。此外，我们扩展了SSM的状态空间以显式映射跨模态空间依赖关系，允许模态间交互增强每个模式的更新。通过将先前隐藏状态的跨模态信息整合到当前状态转换中，TensorSSM有效地沿着两个维度扩展了张量表示：用于粗到细空间标记的序列维度，以及用于跨模态记忆的状态维度。这一设计有效地将空间信息整合到状态空间和张量核心中，大大推进了状态适应性并增强了数据压缩的表达能力。大量实验表明，TensorSSM在不依赖严格空间假设的情况下，在各种张量数据集上实现了极高的重建准确性和存储效率，展现出强健的表达能力。
tldr: TensorSSM是一种基于动态状态空间模型的新型张量压缩方法，通过从粗到细的空间编码和跨模态依赖建模，显著提升了高维张量压缩的准确性与效率。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了一种基于动态状态空间模型（TensorSSM）的方法来处理高维张量压缩，创新性地结合了粗细粒度空间标记和跨模态依赖建模，克服了传统方法将高维张量展平为1D序列所带来的局限性，具有极高的压缩效率和重建准确性。
motivation: 现有的功能性张量分解方法通常将高维张量展平为一维序列，这种折叠操作会导致高度重叠的局部坐标序列，且难以捕捉复杂的跨模态空间依赖性，从而严重限制了其在多样化数据集上的表现力。
method: 提出TensorSSM方法，通过K-ary规则将按模式的坐标分解为序列，以实现从粗到细的空间标记编码；同时扩展SSM的状态空间以显式映射跨模态空间依赖性，实现跨模态交互。
results: 大量实验表明，TensorSSM在各种张量数据集上无需依赖严格的空间假设，即可实现极高的重建准确性和存储效率，展现出强大的表达能力。
conclusion: TensorSSM通过在动态状态空间模型中记忆空间位置和跨模态依赖，解决了传统功能性张量分解方法中空间信息丢失和局部坐标重叠的问题，显著提升了高维张量压缩的表达能力和重建精度。

title: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images
authors: Md Shihabul Islam Shovo, Nishi Kanta Paul, Trung Dong, Xiaomin Lin
abstract: Reliable visual perception is essential for safe autonomous underwater exploration. Yet vision models pretrained on terrestrial images become less reliable underwater, where turbidity, backscatter, and wavelength-dependent attenuation alter scene appearance. Existing adaptation methods either spread adapters equally across the encoder depth or select layers using the divergence between two fixed domains. In this paper, we introduce AquaProbe for measuring how the location of the domain gap changes with water type and imaging range. AquaProbe separates newly introduced divergence from that accumulated through a frozen vision encoder using paired clean and physically rendered images and allocates a fixed LoRA budget according to the measured profile. The segmentation mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) for the proportional LoRA rank allocation, based on the measured profile, is 70.1; this is a better result than uniform LoRA rank allocation by 1.9 mIoU points while having the same parameter budget of 0.59 million adapter parameters. The three-way router, conditioned on estimated condition clusters, achieves 70.6 mIoU on the standard SUIM split and 63.4 AUDRC under held-out degradation.

title: ChatGPT as a Surveillance Assistant? An Exploratory Case Study of AI-Assisted Surveillance Risks
authors: Ayana Hussain, Nicholas Vincent
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate detailed guidance, functional code, and persuasive text at scale. As one of the most widely used consumer language model products as of 2026, ChatGPT gives broad public access to these capabilities, motivating concerns about its potential use in surveillance-related tasks. We present an exploratory case study of what potentially harmful surveillance assistance looks like in ChatGPT's public web interface. We contribute a taxonomy of seven surveillance risk categories based on prior LLM risk research and reports of deployed surveillance systems, instantiated as 110 prompts, along with a manually reviewed analysis of ChatGPT's responses. Prompts were issued using two approaches: 55 jailbreak prompts drawing on five types of elicitation strategies, and 55 plain-language direct prompts, each run alone, and if unsuccessful, again with a short fixed prefix. We find that ChatGPT provides substantive surveillance guidance for 40 of the 55 jailbreak prompts and for 33 of the 55 direct prompts without any prefix. Compliant responses also rarely included policy mentions or suggestions for privacy-preserving alternatives. We manually review every response and find that even when ChatGPT states a refusal, it may still supply detailed instructions, working code, or architectural guidance alongside brief ethical caveats.

title: Qistas: A Pre-Registered, Portable Protocol for Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models
authors: Nawar S. Alseelawi, Mustafa S. Aljumaily
abstract: Fairness benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) are overwhelmingly English-born and American in their social categories; translated versions carry those categories into societies where they do not apply, and almost none fix their hypotheses before the models are run. We present Qistas (Arabic qistas, "the just balance"), a protocol for evaluating how LLMs treat the social, confessional, and regional constituencies of a society, portable across countries and instantiated first for Iraq. In its pilot form it measures only what needs no verdict on contested truth: procedural symmetry across matched counterfactual pairs, differential refusal, stereotype reliance under ambiguity, and terminological framing of documented events. Every measurement is paired by construction and analysed with paired machinery (sign-flip permutation tests, exact McNemar tests, template-clustered bootstrap intervals, Holm-corrected families), with a power analysis that states, before any data exist, the smallest effect each axis can detect after the design effect of template clustering. We release the authoring apparatus (a pruned 3x5 taxonomy with four cells closed by design, per-type checklists, a cumulative rulings log, a structural audit, and a human review notebook) and report its first field test: a semantic review of a 58-item seed bank in which 24 of 25 template groups failed at least one check. The defect patterns it exposed (evaluation criteria leaking into prompts, token-level swaps that break Arabic agreement, epistemically unbalanced pairs, single-theme refusal probes, unwritten dialect twins counted as coverage) are, we argue, general hazards of counterfactual fairness benchmarks. This is a protocol paper, not a results paper: no model has been evaluated, and the accompanying pre-registration commits the hypotheses, metrics, exclusion rules, and analysis plan that the pilot will follow.
comment: 19 pages, 1 figure, 5 tables. Protocol paper; no model results. Pre-registration: https://osf.io/crg5n. Reference implementation: https://github.com/nawaralseelawi/qistas

title: Sparse Autoencoders for Expert-Assisted Interpretation of Histopathology Foundation Model Embeddings
authors: Šimon Šmída, Wanda Benesova
abstract: Histopathology foundation models learn rich embedding representations, but their internal structure remains difficult to inspect. Concept-level interpretability is particularly relevant in computational pathology because pathologists reason through recurring morphological and tissue-level patterns, including tissue architecture, cellular morphology, staining variation, and artifacts. In this work, we investigate whether sparse autoencoders (SAEs) can decompose embeddings from histopathology foundation models into sparse latent features suitable for expert-assisted interpretation. We train vanilla and Batch-TopK SAE variants on NCT-CRC embeddings, using CONCH as the primary foundation model and UNI2-h as an additional robustness evaluation, and characterize the resulting latent features through reconstruction fidelity, sparsity, coherence, label enrichment, and downstream class-signal preservation. The learned sparse representations preserve most downstream tissue-class information, and their latent features retrieve more coherent and label-concentrated patch groups than raw embedding dimensions or PCA components. Discussions with pathology experts further motivated a WSI-level latent visualization workflow that places feature activations into larger tissue context. Overall, the additional UNI2-h evaluation suggests that the observed behavior is not specific to CONCH, supporting the use of sparse autoencoders for expert-assisted analysis of histopathology foundation-model embeddings, while emphasizing that latent features should be treated as candidate concepts requiring pathological assessment rather than automatically validated histopathological concepts.

title: FlapSim: A Composable MuJoCo Simulation Platform and Reduced-Order Aerodynamic Model Hierarchy for Flapping-Wing Robotics
authors: Mingshan He
abstract: Flapping-wing simulation must reconcile high-frequency wingbeat aerodynamics with the slower dynamics relevant to flight control and reinforcement learning. We present FlapSim, a modular open-source MuJoCo simulation platform that combines robot descriptions, wing geometry, and composable aerodynamic models in a deterministic simulation pipeline. Across $48$ held-out scenarios spanning frequency, gimbal, wind, frequency-step, gust, and cross-robot flat-plate regimes, we compare five reduced-order configurations operating at $1\,\text{ms}$ with a $50\,μ\text{s}$ quasi-steady blade-element reference. The built-in hover cycle-averaged baseline achieves a $67.51\times$ CPU speedup but only $0.6593$ mean wrench fidelity. Combining multirate $21$-substep clock synchronization, three-dimensional linear/quadratic inflow and gust coupling, analytical blade-element geometry scaling, and phase-locked $1f\text{--}6f$ harmonics raises mean fidelity to $0.9646$ at a $65.19\times$ speedup in a five-block model. A streamlined four-block model without explicit step-transient lag states achieves $0.9662$ fidelity at a $67.98\times$ speedup. Controlled ablations show that stroke harmonics are particularly important during frequency transitions, improving held-out frequency-step fidelity by $+0.3176$. Transfer-function analysis explains this effect: fixed-window cycle averaging retains harmonic contributions when the wingbeat frequency changes, so within-cycle reconstruction also improves the filtered wrench. Once phase alignment and harmonic synthesis are included, explicit transient lag states provide no additional benefit in this benchmark. These results characterize the accuracy--computation tradeoff of the aerodynamic hierarchy and identify timing, inflow, geometry, and harmonic representation as central considerations for reduced-order flapping-wing simulation.

title: TSFLab: A Self-Improving Agent-Agnostic Workbench for Time Series Forecasting Research
authors: ChengAo Shen, Yanjun Zhao, Haoxin Liu, Bonnie Chen, Miles Ma, Dongjin Song, Hanghang Tong, Qingsong Wen, Jingrui He, Jingchao Ni
abstract: As publications and products on time series forecasting (TSF) proliferate, researchers face a growing burden of analyzing existing work. First, not all publications release code. For instance, only about 20% of arXiv TSF papers have a code link in the surveyed period. Second, released code also requires manual maintenance. Thus, TSF researchers must constantly adapt or implement existing works. However, independent implementations can differ in experimental settings and are difficult to maintain. We therefore propose to use AI agents for benchmarking TSF research and even supporting autoresearch, e.g., developing new TSF models. Yet directly applying existing coding agents, such as Claude Code and Codex, is suboptimal: prohibitive costs, limited scalability to large research projects (e.g., benchmarking), and lack of self-maintenance. To address these challenges, we propose TSFLab, a self-improving agent-agnostic "workbench" that equips compatible coding agents with shared resources and tools for low-cost TSF research and continuous maintenance of research resources. Our experiments cover reproduction, benchmarking, and new method development. In reproduction and benchmarking, TSFLab improves task completion by 20-163% and cuts fresh tokens per completed task by 11-66% across baselines. A pilot study of agent-driven method development also shows improved forecasting accuracy via TSFLab, with 32.8-73.6% fewer fresh tokens and 9.2-68.8% less development time than the other settings.

title: Does Recursive Knowledge Construction Help Agents Verify Consensus Claims in Science?
authors: Lun Ai, Yu-Heng Wu, Jonathan Schaul, Leonie Küchenhoff, Denes Turei, Francesco Carli, Fabio Petroni, Aurelien Dugourd, Julio Saez-Rodriguez
abstract: Recent scientific agents build knowledge recursively by retrieving evidence, constructing an intermediate state, and judging whether that state contains sufficient information. These agents are evaluated end-to-end, usually without ground truth, so the effect of each design choice is unknown. Here, we examined two design axes: (1) what the recursion builds (the state of evidence) and (2) what controls it (the judge that decides when to stop). To measure them, we defined consensus scientific claim verification and measured these effects on this task, where a system must establish a claim's consensus stance from the open literature. We built a new consensus claim dataset, ProClaim-eval, including 718 claims with SUPPORT and REFUTE gold labels from five expert-curated databases spanning molecular biology, nuclear physics, and astronomy. Our instrument, ProClaim, persists an evidence state outside the model's context, so each axis can be studied with the other held fixed. Against verification systems and general-purpose agent harnesses, ProClaim ranks among the top three, with a significant advantage over the harnesses. We found that the evidence state improves performance over in-context accumulation, and it also matters what is stored in it. In addition, a trained judge that reads the evidence state performs better than fixed-round stopping. A judge trained separately and never exposed to ProClaim-eval achieves the highest agreement with the gold labels on three of five subsets, where it matches the off-the-shelf Claude Sonnet~4.6 judge and outperforms Claude Haiku~4.5. Our results support recursively maintaining a structured evidence state outside the model's context as an effective design for verifying claims in scientific agents.
zh_title: 递归知识构建是否有助于智能体验证科学领域的共识主张？
translation: 近期科学智能体通过检索证据、构建中间状态以及判断该状态是否包含充分信息来递归地构建知识。这些智能体通常在缺乏基准真值的情况下进行端到端评估，因此各个设计选择的具体影响尚不明确。在此，我们考察了两个设计维度：（1）递归所构建的内容（证据状态）以及（2）控制递归的机制（决定何时停止的判定器）。为了衡量它们，我们定义了科学共识主张验证任务并测量了这些因素在该任务上的效果，在该任务中系统必须从公开文献中确立某项主张的共识立场。我们构建了一个新的共识主张数据集 ProClaim-eval，包含来自跨分子生物学、核物理学和天文学的五个专家策展数据库的 718 条具有“支持（SUPPORT）”和“反驳（REFUTE）”黄金标签的主张。我们的工具 ProClaim 将证据状态持久化在模型上下文之外，从而可以在保持另一个维度固定的情况下独立研究每个维度。与现有验证系统和通用智能体框架相比，ProClaim 跻身前三，且明显优于通用框架。我们发现证据状态比上下文内累积更能提升性能，并且其中存储的内容也至关重要。此外，读取证据状态的受训判定器表现优于固定轮次停止。一个单独训练且从未接触过 ProClaim-eval 的判定器在五个子集中的三个上与黄金标签达成最高一致性，与现成的 Claude Sonnet 4.6 判定器表现相当，并超越了 Claude Haiku 4.5。我们的结果支持在模型上下文之外递归维护结构化证据状态，并将其作为科学智能体中验证主张的有效设计。
tldr: 研究证实，在模型上下文之外递归维护结构化的证据状态并配合专门的停止判定器，能显著提升科学智能体验证科学共识声明的能力。
ai_comments: 该论文敏锐地指出了当前科学智能体端到端评估中因缺乏细粒度基准真值而导致具体模块设计效果不明的局限。其创新性在于系统性地解耦并实证了“外部状态存储”与“终止判定器”两个关键设计维度，并通过多学科专家策展数据构建了扎实的评测集，为科学领域大模型智能体的状态管理与控制架构提供了重要指导。
motivation: 当前科学智能体通常在缺乏基准真值的情况下进行端到端评估，导致递归构建知识时“构建的内容（证据状态）”与“控制机制（判定器）”等不同设计选择的实际效用尚不明确。
method: 定义了科学共识声明验证任务，并构建了跨三个学科、包含718条金标声明的基准数据集 ProClaim-eval；提出 ProClaim 系统，将证据状态持久化存储在模型上下文之外，以控制变量的方式分别评估证据状态构建方式与终止判定机制。
results: ProClaim 性能跻身对比系统前三且显著超越通用智能体框架；上下文外的证据状态优于上下文内累积，且其存储内容显著影响效果；受训判定器优于固定轮次停止，其泛化判定器在3/5的子集上达成最高一致性，性能匹敌 Claude Sonnet 4.6 并优于 Claude Haiku 4.5。
conclusion: 在模型上下文之外递归维护结构化的证据状态，并配合读取该状态的判定器，是科学智能体有效验证共识声明的有效架构设计。

title: Coupled or Independent? Fault Coupling in Agentic Medical Vision Systems
authors: Nishi Kanta Paul, Md Shihabul Islam Shovo, Md Mostafijur Rahman, Jamil Fayyad
abstract: Vision-language agents equipped with tools expose intermediate outputs for inspection and comparison with the model's reasoning, which may offer safety benefits over single-shot models. This paper tests that potential benefit when the sensor reading itself is untrusted, so that the tool and reasoning channels share a common visual fault. We consider a dermatology agent based on segmentation, contrastive retrieval, and an iterative vision-language reasoner and define a coupling taxonomy that distinguishes single-channel errors from joint errors that agree or disagree. On PAD-UFES-20, we show that typographic injection produces detectable directional retrieval capture, whereas physical corruption does not. Crop-first retrieval preserves the payload at a readable scale and produces 55% joint wrong agreement across all cases (71% of faulty cases); full-image retrieval produces 35% (43%). Under a binary decision, if both channels are wrong, their predictions must agree, so hard-label channel comparison cannot detect joint failures, limiting disagreement recall to 0.29 (crop-first) versus 0.57 (full-image). The direction of the order effect is reproduced on the independent HIBA test set.
zh_title: 耦合还是独立？代理式医疗视觉系统中的故障耦合
translation: 配备工具的视觉-语言代理暴露中间输出以供检查和与模型推理进行比较，这可能比单次模型提供安全优势。当传感器读数本身不可信时，本论文测试了这种潜在优势，因此工具和推理通道共享一个共同的视觉故障。我们考虑了一个基于分割、对比检索和迭代视觉-语言推理器的皮肤病代理，并定义了一个耦合分类法，该分类法区分了单通道错误和一致或不一致的联合错误。在PAD-UFES-20数据集上，我们发现排版注入产生可检测的方向性检索捕获，而物理损坏则不能。裁剪优先检索以可读的比例保留了有效载荷，并在所有情况下产生55%的联合错误一致性（71%的故障情况）；全图像检索产生35%（43%）。在二元决策下，如果两个通道都错误，它们的预测必须一致，因此硬标签通道比较无法检测联合故障，将不一致召回率限制在0.29（裁剪优先）对0.57（全图像）。顺序效应的方向在独立的HIBA测试集上得到重现。
tldr: 研究了当传感器读数不可信时，代理式医疗视觉系统中工具和推理通道的故障耦合，发现硬标签通道比较难以检测联合故障。
ai_comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于提出了代理式医疗视觉系统中故障耦合的概念，并定义了相应的分类法，这对于理解和提升这类系统的安全性至关重要。研究揭示了在传感器读数不可信的实际场景中，多通道系统可能存在的盲点，即硬标签比较难以检测到工具和推理通道同时出错的联合故障。这对于未来设计更鲁棒、更能自我诊断的医疗AI系统具有重要指导意义，尤其是在需要高可靠性的医疗诊断领域。
motivation: 探索视觉-语言代理在传感器读数不可信时，通过暴露中间输出进行检查和比较，是否能提供比单次模型更高的安全性。
method: 构建了一个基于分割、对比检索和迭代视觉-语言推理器的皮肤病代理。定义了一个区分单通道错误和联合错误的耦合分类法。在PAD-UFES-20数据集上，通过排版注入和物理损坏测试了故障，并比较了裁剪优先检索和全图像检索的效果。
results: 排版注入产生可检测的方向性检索捕获，而物理损坏则不能。裁剪优先检索在所有情况下产生55%的联合错误一致性（71%的故障情况）；全图像检索产生35%（43%）。硬标签通道比较无法检测联合故障，将不一致召回率限制在0.29（裁剪优先）对0.57（全图像）。顺序效应的方向在独立的HIBA测试集上得到重现。
conclusion: 硬标签通道比较无法有效检测代理式医疗视觉系统中工具和推理通道的联合故障，限制了不一致召回率。

title: No Channels Left Behind: Understanding Diffusion Acceleration through Residual Gates
authors: Junha Park, Jaemyung Yu, Jaehui Hwang, Jong-Seok Lee, Dongyoon Han
abstract: Training acceleration methods for diffusion transformers, such as REPA and dispersive regularization, are commonly explained by additional supervision, spatial-structure priors, or improved feature geometry. We revisit this view and uncover a striking internal change: the AdaLN-Zero residual gate $α$, which directly controls how conditioned updates enter the residual stream, is substantially reorganized by these methods. This observation motivates our hypothesis that acceleration arises, at least in part, from reshaping the residual gating pathway rather than solely from the feature structures explicitly imposed by auxiliary objectives. Supporting this view, accelerated models are markedly more sensitive to perturbations of $α$, and their gate geometry reflects semantic relationships among classes. We further introduce the normalized participation ratio (nPR) to characterize the channel-wise organization of the gates and find that, across REPA teachers, projector architectures, and radial-objective targets, broader gate participation accompanies better generation quality. Guided by this insight, we propose a simple teacher-free radial objective that promotes broader gate participation through feature-norm regularization, without pairwise feature comparisons. On ImageNet $256\times256$ with SiT-B/2, our method improves FID over dispersive loss while increasing mean gate participation over timesteps and classes, further supporting the link between gate organization and training acceleration. Our results identify residual-gate reorganization as a measurable axis of diffusion training acceleration and suggest a simple direction for further acceleration.
zh_title: 不遗漏任何通道：通过残差门理解扩散加速
translation: 扩散Transformer的训练加速方法，如REPA和分散正则化，通常通过额外的监督、空间结构先验或改进的特征几何来解释。我们重新审视了这一观点，并揭示了一个惊人的内部变化：AdaLN-Zero残差门α，它直接控制条件更新如何进入残差流，被这些方法大幅重组。这一观察促使我们提出假设，即加速至少部分源于残差门控路径的重塑，而不仅仅是辅助目标明确施加的显式特征结构。为了支持这一观点，加速模型对α的扰动明显更敏感，并且它们的门几何结构反映了类别间的语义关系。我们进一步引入了归一化参与率（nPR）来表征门的通道组织，并发现，在REPA教师、投影仪架构和径向目标中，更广泛的门参与伴随着更好的生成质量。受此启发，我们提出了一种简单的无教师径向目标，通过特征范数正则化促进更广泛的门参与，而无需成对特征比较。在ImageNet $256	imes256$与SiT-B/2上，我们的方法在提高时间步和类别上的平均门参与度的同时，改善了相对于分散损失的FID，进一步支持了门组织与训练加速之间的联系。我们的结果将残差门重组确定为扩散训练加速的一个可衡量维度，并为进一步加速提供了一个简单的方向。
tldr: 扩散加速方法通过重组残差门（AdaLN-Zero α）而非仅通过显式特征结构来工作，这提高了生成质量。本文引入了归一化参与率（nPR）并提出了一个促进更广泛门参与的无教师径向目标，在ImageNet上显著提升了FID。
ai_comments: 本文提供了一个理解扩散模型训练加速的新颖视角，将关注点从外部监督和特征结构转移到模型内部的残差门控机制。引入归一化参与率（nPR）和提出无教师径向目标是重要的贡献，为优化扩散模型提供了可量化且实用的方法。这项研究对于深入理解扩散Transformer的工作原理及其加速潜力具有重要意义。
motivation: 扩散Transformer的训练加速方法通常被解释为额外的监督、空间结构先验或改进的特征几何。本文重新审视了这一观点，并发现了一个显著的内部变化：AdaLN-Zero残差门α被这些方法大幅重组。这促使作者假设加速至少部分源于残差门控路径的重塑，而不仅仅是辅助目标明确施加的特征结构。
method: 本文引入了归一化参与率（nPR）来表征门的通道组织。基于此洞察，提出了一种简单的无教师径向目标，通过特征范数正则化促进更广泛的门参与，而无需成对特征比较。
results: 加速模型对α的扰动明显更敏感，且其门几何结构反映了类别间的语义关系。研究发现，在REPA教师、投影仪架构和径向目标中，更广泛的门参与伴随着更好的生成质量。在ImageNet $256	imes256$与SiT-B/2上，本文的方法在提高平均门参与度的同时，改善了相对于分散损失的FID。
conclusion: 本文结果将残差门重组确定为扩散训练加速的一个可衡量维度，并为进一步加速提供了一个简单的方向。

title: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness
authors: Nicolas Gertler, Claudio Novelli, Luciano Floridi
abstract: Large language models act only through the infrastructure that surrounds them. That infrastructure, the harness, determines what a model can accomplish and how it fails, yet it has no settled definition. To address this gap, we decompose the harness into eight functional components that can be specified and compared across systems, and we propose a portable specification framework that records which model ran in which harness. The record is needed because different harness configurations can yield several-fold differences in reported scores for the same model, and because much of an agent's attack surface lies in its harness. Existing model cards and agent cards provide release and operational information, but do not establish the sequence of effective configurations within a run. Harnesses can change between releases and between runs, and, where agents edit their own tools and configuration, within a run. Enacted AI laws contain documentation duties relevant to covered systems, subject to their respective scopes and application dates, but do not prescribe the common harness record proposed here. Therefore, the harness has to be explicitly described and specified as a versioned part of the system.
zh_title: 迈向智能体运行支撑框架的可移植规范
translation: 大语言模型仅通过其周围的基础设施发挥作用。这种基础设施即Harness（运行支撑框架），决定了模型能够完成什么以及如何失败，但它目前还没有固定的定义。为了填补这一空白，我们将Harness分解为八个功能组件，以便在不同系统之间进行规范和比较，并提出了一种可移植的规范框架，用于记录哪个模型在哪个Harness中运行。之所以需要这种记录，是因为不同的Harness配置会导致同一模型的报告得分出现数倍差异，而且智能体的大部分攻击面都存在于其Harness中。现有的模型卡和智能体卡提供了发布和运行信息，但并未确立单次运行中有效配置的序列。Harness可能会在不同版本之间、不同运行之间发生变化，并且在智能体自行编辑工具和配置的情况下，还会在运行过程中发生变化。已颁布的AI法律包含与受涵盖系统相关的文档记录义务，但并未规定本文所提出的通用Harness记录。因此，Harness必须作为系统的一个版本化部分进行显式描述和规范。
tldr: 该论文提出将大语言模型智能体的运行基础设施（Harness）分解为八个组件，并采用可移植的规范框架来记录配置，以解决因基础设施不同导致模型性能差异巨大及安全审计困难的问题。
ai_comments: 该论文切中了大模型智能体（Agent）研究中的一个盲点：以往的研究高度关注模型本身，而忽视了其运行基础设施（Harness）对性能和安全性的决定性影响。通过提出八大功能组件和一个可移植的规范框架，该研究为AI系统的可复现性、基准测试公平性以及安全审计提供了重要基础。
motivation: 大语言模型的效果严重依赖于其周围的基础设施（即Harness），但目前该基础设施缺乏统一的定义、记录标准和可移植的规范，而不同的Harness配置会导致模型性能评分出现数倍差异且存在安全隐患。
method: 将智能体运行支撑框架（Harness）分解为八个功能组件，并在系统间进行规范与比较；同时提出一个可移植的规范框架，用于记录特定模型在特定支撑框架下的运行情况。
results: 不同的Harness配置会导致同一模型的报告得分出现数倍差异；现有的模型卡和智能体卡无法记录运行中的配置序列；提出的通用Harness记录和规范框架能够填补这一空白，满足AI法律对文档记录的需求。
conclusion: 为了准确评估大语言模型智能体的性能并保障其安全性，必须将运行支撑框架（Harness）作为系统版本化的重要组成部分进行明确描述和规范。

title: Approximate Dynamic Programming for Link Reconfiguration to Reduce Malicious Input Controllability in Consensus Networks
authors: Nathaniel Mailhot, Mohammad Pirani, Davide Spinello
abstract: Communication links influence how strongly a malicious input at one sensor affects a consensus network. We study how a defender can reduce this influence by selecting one additional link after observing the currently attacked sensor. The attacked sensor changes over time, and vulnerability is measured by the trace of a finite-horizon controllability Gramian. A prescribed local epsilon-greedy attacker response rule defines a discounted Markov decision process for the defender. Exact dynamic programming (DP) provides an optimal policy using the full Gramian payoff matrix and attacker transition model. We then introduce approximate dynamic programming (ADP) that learns from sampled attacker transitions and empirical Gramian costs estimated from measured impulse responses. Under conditionally unbiased costs and standard sampling and learning-rate conditions, the learned action-value table converges to the exact DP solution. The analysis uses Bellman contraction and bounds the effect of persistent Gramian estimation bias, establishing when measured responses recover optimal defender decisions without constructing the full payoff matrix. In simulations on 20- and 100-node graphs, empirical ADP rollout costs are within 0.23% and 1.76%, respectively, of exact DP. In a two-dimensional intruder tracking example, both policies reduce network-wide root-mean-square tracking error spread by approximately 25% relative to an unmitigated attack.
zh_title: 用于链路重构以减少共识网络中恶意输入可控性的近似动态规划
translation: 通信链路影响着共识网络中某个传感器上的恶意输入的影响强度。我们研究了防御者如何在观察到当前受攻击的传感器后，通过选择一条额外的链路来减利这种影响。受攻击的传感器随时间变化，脆弱性通过有限期可控性格拉姆矩阵的迹来衡量。规定的局部 epsilon-greedy 攻击者响应规则为防御者定义了一个折扣马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）。精确动态规划（DP）利用完整的 Gramian 收益矩阵和攻击者转移模型提供最优策略。随后，我们引入了近似动态规划（ADP），它通过采样的攻击者转移和从测得的脉冲响应估计的经验 Gramian 成本来进行学习。在条件无偏成本以及标准的采样和学习率条件下，所学习的动作-价值表收敛到精确的 DP 解。分析利用了贝尔曼压缩并限制了持续 Gramian 估计偏差的影响，确定了在不构建完整收益矩阵的情况下，测得的响应何时能恢复最优的防御者决策。在 20 节点和 100 节点图的仿真中，经验 ADP rollout 成本分别在精确 DP 的 0.23% 和 1.76% 以内。在二维入侵者追踪示例中，与未缓解的攻击相比，这两种策略都将网络范围的均方根追踪误差分布减少了约 25%。
tldr: 本文提出了一种近似动态规划（ADP）方法，用于在共识网络中动态选择通信链路，以有效减小恶意攻击的影响，计算性能接近最优解。
ai_comments: 该论文将近似动态规划（ADP）引入共识网络中恶意输入可控性的链路重构问题，创新性地结合了强化学习/抽样机制与控制理论，在保证理论收敛性的同时大大降低了计算复杂度，仿真结果也证明了其高效性。
motivation: 为了减少共识网络中由于传感器受到恶意攻击而产生的控制力影响，防御者需要通过选择额外的通信链路来进行动态重构，而传统的精确动态规划方法计算复杂度高，因此需要一种基于采样和测量的近似动态规划方法。
method: 建立折扣马尔可夫决策过程，提出近似动态规划（ADP）算法，通过采样的攻击者转移和从测得的脉冲响应中估计的经验Gramian成本进行学习，并利用Bellman压缩映射证明了收敛性。
results: 在20节点和100节点的图仿真中，经验ADP的 rollout 成本分别在精确DP的 0.23% 和 1.76% 以内；在二维入侵者追踪示例中，两个策略均能将全网均方根追踪误差分布减少约25%。
conclusion: 论文成功提出了一种基于近似动态规划的链路重构方法，能够在未知或复杂攻击转换模型下有效减小恶意输入的影响，具有良好的理论收敛性与实践效果。

title: Robot Navigation and Canine Welfare: A Pilot Study Surfacing Challenges for Cross-Species Legibility and Proxy Validity in Animal-Machine Interaction
authors: Haoxiang Zhang, Nancy Smith
abstract: Autonomous delivery robots increasingly share residential spaces with companion animals, yet navigation behavior is rarely designed with animal welfare in mind. This paper presents a pilot study evaluating a curve-out maneuver, a laterally arcing pass-by trajectory triggered at the dog's alert distance, proposed as a candidate welfare-informed navigation intervention grounded in canine social communication research and legible motion theory. Following a research through design approach, we developed and evaluated a first design iteration of the artifact in a naturalistic home environment with a companion dog. Contrary to our hypothesis, the curve-out produced a more acute stress response than the straight-line baseline. We argue that discontinuous execution limitation, the robot stopping and reorienting multiple times to approximate the arc, undermined legibility, which in itself became a stressor. The pilot surfaces the legibility of robot behavior to non-humans' eyes and proxy stimulus validity as structural challenges for AMI and repositions the design problem for future work.
zh_title: 机器人导航与犬类福利：一项初步研究揭示跨物种可理解性和代理有效性在动物-机器交互中的挑战
translation: 自动配送机器人越来越多地与伴侣动物共享居住空间，然而导航行为很少在设计时考虑动物福利。本文提出了一项初步研究，评估了一种“弧线避让”策略——一种在狗的警觉距离触发的横向弧形通过轨迹，该策略被提议作为一种基于犬类社会交流研究和可理解运动理论的、以福利为导向的导航干预措施。我们采用“设计研究”方法，在一个自然家庭环境中与一只伴侣犬开发并评估了该人工制品的首次设计迭代。与我们的假设相反，“弧线避让”策略比直线通过基线产生了更严重的应激反应。我们认为，不连续的执行限制，即机器人多次停顿和重新定位以近似弧线，损害了可理解性，这本身就成为了一个压力源。这项初步研究揭示了机器人行为对非人类的可理解性以及代理刺激的有效性是动物-机器交互中的结构性挑战，并重新定位了未来工作的设计问题。
tldr: 机器人为照顾犬类福利设计的“弧线避让”策略反而增加了犬类压力，因为其不连续的执行损害了可理解性。
ai_comments: 这项初步研究非常重要，因为它首次直接探讨了机器人导航行为对伴侣动物福利的影响，并挑战了直观上认为的“友好”设计。其创新之处在于将犬类社会交流理论引入机器人导航设计，并揭示了“可理解性”这一关键因素在跨物种交互中的复杂性。研究结果强调了在设计动物-机器交互时，需要深入理解动物的感知和认知，而不仅仅是人类的直觉。局限性在于这是一项初步研究，样本量可能较小，且仅测试了一种特定的“弧线避让”策略及其执行方式。
motivation: 自动配送机器人与伴侣动物共享居住空间，但机器人导航行为很少考虑动物福利。
method: 本研究采用“设计研究”方法，开发并评估了一种“弧线避让”策略（一种在狗的警觉距离触发的横向弧形通过轨迹），并在自然家庭环境中与一只伴侣犬进行了初步研究。
results: 与假设相反，“弧线避让”策略比直线通过基线产生了更严重的应激反应。研究认为，机器人不连续的执行（多次停顿和重新定位以近似弧线）损害了可理解性，这本身就成为了一个压力源。
conclusion: 这项初步研究揭示了机器人行为对非人类的可理解性以及代理刺激的有效性是动物-机器交互中的结构性挑战，并重新定位了未来工作的设计问题。

title: Confidence-Modulated Safety Filtering for End-to-End Policies
authors: Javier Borquez, Jaime F. Fisac
abstract: End-to-end policies, from task-specific controllers to robot foundation models, learn complex behavior from raw observations but are not guaranteed to remain safe, so they are often wrapped in a safety filter. The resulting system operates under two domains: the filter's operational design domain (ODD), where its assumptions hold and safety is certified, and the policy's competence domain, where it is reliable. Filters typically fix their conservativeness regardless of the policy's competence, trading performance inside the ODD against margin beyond it. We ask whether the policy's confidence should set that level, and propose a filter-agnostic pipeline that modulates it at runtime: inside the ODD, where every setting is safe, confidence buys performance; beyond it, low confidence adds margin, which helps when it flags where the filter's model fails. Preliminary F1TENTH simulations, where this holds, show the modulated filter combining the strengths of permissive and conservative filters.
zh_title: 端到端策略的置信度调制安全过滤
translation: 从特定任务控制器到机器人基础模型的端到端策略，能够从原始观测中学习复杂行为，但无法保证始终安全，因此通常需要外包一层安全过滤器。由此产生的系统在两个域下运行：过滤器假设成立且安全得到认证的操作设计域（ODD），以及策略可靠的能力域。过滤器的保守性通常是固定的，无论策略的能力如何，都在ODD内部的性能与ODD外部的安全余量之间进行权衡。我们探讨了是否应该由策略的置信度来设定该保守水平，并提出了一种与过滤器无关的流水线，在运行期对其进行调制：在ODD内部（此处每个设置都是安全的），置信度换取性能；在ODD外部，低置信度增加了安全余量，这在标记过滤器模型失效的地方非常有用。初步的F1TENTH仿真表明，调制后的过滤器结合了宽松过滤器和保守过滤器的优势。
tldr: 提出了一种利用端到端策略运行置信度来动态调整安全过滤器保守性的方法，从而在保证安全的同时优化了系统性能。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的置信度调制安全过滤方法，将策略的运行置信度与安全过滤器的保守性动态绑定，成功兼顾了ODD内外的性能与安全性，具有很高的实用价值和通用性。
motivation: 传统的安全过滤器无论端到端策略的胜任能力如何，其保守性都是固定的，这导致在操作设计域（ODD）内外的性能与安全余量权衡不够灵活。因此，需要研究是否应由策略的置信度来决定安全过滤器的保守程度。
method: 提出了一种与具体过滤器无关的运行期管理流水线，利用策略的置信度来动态调节安全过滤器的保守性水平。
results: 初步的F1TENTH仿真结果表明，经过置信度调制的安全过滤器成功结合了宽松过滤器和保守过滤器的优点。
conclusion: 通过引入置信度调制，安全过滤器能够在ODD内部利用高置信度提升性能，在ODD外部通过低置信度增加安全余量，从而在F1TENTH仿真中展现出结合了宽松和保守过滤器优势的出色表现。

title: CoFiBreak: A Coarse-to-Fine Diversity Reward for Effective Multi-Turn Jailbreak
authors: Jialin Song, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang, Mingqian Feng, Chengquan Guo, Qiyao Ma, Carolyn Buractaon, Anson Ho, Wuyang Chen, Christopher White
abstract: Automated red teaming trains an attacker large language model (LLM) to elicit harmful responses from a victim LLM, but reinforcement learning can collapse attackers onto a narrow set of prompts when attack success is the only reward. Such a collapse of attack diversity can bias safety evaluation toward repeatedly testing near-duplicate attack patterns rather than the underlying harmful intents. Existing methods often trade off attack success or inference cost for greater content or strategy diversity. We propose CoFiBreak, a coarse-to-fine diversity reward for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that improves attack diversity while preserving strong attack effectiveness and low inference cost. The coarse reward broadens which strategies the attacker uses by encouraging strategies underrepresented within each GRPO group, while the fine reward broadens how those strategies are realized by discouraging reuse of the same personas, framings, and output formats after harmful-intent information is removed from prompt embeddings. Diversity rewards apply only to attacks that already exceed an effectiveness threshold, so diversity cannot be gained through ineffective attacks. Since both rewards are computed only during training, CoFiBreak also retains inference efficiency. Trained with Llama3.1-8B-Instruct as the victim, CoFiBreak discovers 1.6-2.0x as many distinct successful fine-grained strategies as the strongest baseline across frontier victims on HarmBench. It reaches 98.8% ASR@10 (attack success rate with 10 generations per intent) on AdvBench with the highest diversity score among all compared methods, which is 2.1x that of the strongest-attacking baseline. The resulting attacks transfer to unseen frontier LLMs, reaching 71.0% ASR@10 on AdvBench with the unseen victim Claude-Opus-4.6. The code will be released.
comment: 10 pages main text, 24 pages total, 8 figures, 12 tables
zh_title: CoFiBreak：用于有效多轮越狱的粗到精多样性奖励机制
translation: 自动红蓝对抗训练一个攻击者大语言模型（LLM）来从受害者LLM中诱导有害响应，但当攻击成功是唯一的奖励时，强化学习会导致攻击者收敛到一组狭隘的提示词上。这种攻击多样性的崩溃会使安全评估偏向于重复测试近乎重复的攻击模式，而不是底层的有害意图。现有方法通常以牺牲攻击成功率或推理成本为代价来换取更大的内容或策略多样性。我们提出了CoFiBreak，这是一种用于群组相对策略优化（GRPO）的粗到精多样性奖励，它在保持强大的攻击有效性和低推理成本的同时，提高了攻击多样性。粗糙奖励通过鼓励GRPO组内代表性不足的策略来拓宽攻击者使用的策略，而精细奖励在从提示词嵌入中去除有害意图信息后，通过阻止重复使用相同的角色、框架和输出格式来拓宽这些策略的实现方式。多样性奖励仅适用于已经超过有效性阈值的攻击，因此无法通过无效攻击获得多样性。由于这两种奖励仅在训练期间计算，CoFiBreak还保留了推理效率。使用Llama3.1-8B-Instruct作为受害者进行训练，CoFiBreak在HarmBench上发现了跨前沿受害者最强基线的1.6-2.0倍的独特成功细粒度策略。它在AdvBench上达到了98.8%的ASR@10（每个意图生成10次的攻击成功率），并在所有比较方法中拥有最高的多样性得分，是攻击最强基线的2.1倍。由此产生的攻击可以转移到未见过的先进LLM上，在未见过的受害者Claude-Opus-4.6上的AdvBench上达到了71.0%的ASR@10。代码将被开源。
tldr: 本文提出了一种名为CoFiBreak的粗到精多样性奖励机制，解决了大语言模型自动红蓝对抗中的攻击多样性崩溃问题，实现了高攻击成功率、高多样性且不增加推理成本。
ai_comments: CoFiBreak创新性地将粗到精的多样性奖励引入到大模型自动红蓝对抗和越狱攻击中，有效解决了传统强化学习中攻击模式单一化的问题，同时保持了高攻击成功率和推理效率。
motivation: 自动化红蓝对抗在仅使用攻击成功作为奖励时，强化学习容易导致攻击者陷入狭隘的提示词集合，造成攻击多样性崩溃，使安全评估偏向于重复测试相近的攻击模式，而忽视了底层的有害意图。
method: 提出CoFiBreak，一种基于群组相对策略优化（GRPO）的粗到精多样性奖励方法。粗糙奖励通过鼓励GRPO组内代表性不足的策略来拓宽攻击策略；精细奖励通过在移除有害意图信息后惩罚重复的角色、框架和输出格式，来拓宽策略的实现方式。仅对超过有效性阈值的攻击施加多样性奖励，且奖励仅在训练时计算。
results: 在HarmBench上，CoFiBreak发现的独特成功细粒度策略是效用最强基线的1.6-2.0倍；在AdvBench上达到了98.8%的ASR@10，多样性得分是攻击最强基线的2.1倍；生成的攻击能够迁移到未见过的先进LLM（如Claude-Opus-4.6），在AdvBench上达到71.0%的ASR@10。
conclusion: CoFiBreak通过粗到精的多样性奖励机制，成功解决了大语言模型自动化红蓝对抗中的策略单一化问题，在保持高攻击成功率和推理效率的同时，显著提升了攻击的多样性和泛化能力。

title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
authors: Wendi Li, Huseyin A. Inan, Wei-Ning Chen, Yanzhi Chen, Chetan Bansal, Saravan Rajmohan, Sharon Li
abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model agents by sampling and selecting among multiple candidate trajectories, but common realizations assume that these trajectories can be executed in parallel. This assumption breaks in realistic deployments, where enterprise workspaces and cloud services are shared and persistent, costly or infeasible to replicate, and actions may introduce irreversible side effects or cross-trajectory interference. Existing generative world models avoid direct execution, but typically compress environment state into a single prompt, limiting their ability to reliably simulate transitions under partial observability. Instead, we introduce Agentic World Modeling (AWM), which reformulates next-observation prediction as a multi-turn evidence-acquisition task. For each hypothetical action, an agentic simulator adaptively queries the real environment through safe read-only interfaces, reasons over the returned evidence, and uses executable computation to construct the resulting observation without mutating shared state. Integrated with trajectory-level TTS, AWM enables parallel exploration over a single shared environment. Across $τ$-bench, AppWorld, and OfficeBench, AWM outperforms a single-shot simulation baseline by 40.07% on average, and surpasses a trained world-model baseline by 12.36% on average. These results establish interactive, read-grounded simulation as a practical foundation for safe and scalable agentic test-time scaling in shared, non-resettable environments.

title: LiHA: Worse is Better for Lightweight Hash-based Source Authentication
authors: Negin Dehghanchaleshtori, Homit Dalia, Himanshu Chandra, Rohan Tripathi, Marc E. Fiuczynski, Richard P. Martin
abstract:
The omission of source IP authentication remains a fundamental vulnerability in the Internet. Existing approaches rely on routing plausibility, topology assumptions, per-flow state, or wide deployment. These requirements have kept strong source authentication out of the data plane.
  As simplicity is the key to deployability, we present LiHA, a lightweight source authentication mechanism built around operations that routers already perform efficiently. LiHA binds secret keys to source prefixes using longest prefix match and authenticates each packet with a single message authentication code (MAC). The data plane requires no handshakes, per-flow state, or per-packet control plane access. A sender performs one prefix lookup and one fixed-size hash. The verifier repeats the same operations and forwards the packet only if the MAC matches.
  LiHA is designed for incremental deployment. It primarily protects against off-path attackers that spoof source prefixes they do not control. An on-path attacker can replay valid authenticated packets until the key rotates. LiHA does not eliminate every denial-of-service threat. Instead, it confines accepted traffic to authenticated source prefix space within participating networks. We argue that simpler source authentication with clear limits is more likely to be deployed.
  We implemented LiHA in three environments: as a set of user-space libraries, as eBPF programs, and in an FPGA. We found that the user-space implementation had very high overheads. The eBPF implementation got reasonable single thread performance even with a software based cryptographic hash. We found that only the FPGA could obtain 100 Gbps single thread performance, but that was only when bypassing the kernel using a DPDK user-level networking stack.

title: Adaptive Personalization Under Preference Epistemic Uncertainty
authors: Priyanka Dey, Rajarshi Das, Vikas Bahirwani, Qi Zeng, Julia Kruk, Qi Qi
abstract: Human preferences change over time: an established preference may remain valid over time, become uncertain as context shifts, or be explicitly revised. Effective personalization requires conversational AI to adapt its response strategy to evolving preferences rather than relying on passive memory retrieval. We formalize this capability as adaptive personalization under epistemic uncertainty. A human preference study further confirms that people favor state-contingent response strategies as preference uncertainty changes. To evaluate whether language models mirror this adaptation, we create a multilingual benchmark spanning 250 personas, 5 languages, and 25K conversational turns that decouples strategy selection from response execution. Across eight closed- and open-weight models, we uncover a recognition-generation gap: models reliably identify appropriate strategies when selecting among candidate options, but collapse during open-ended generation, suffering a 35-46% drop in strategy calibration. Crucially, this failure is systematic: models default to exploit-first behavior, over-relying on existing preferences regardless of preference epistemic uncertainty. We show this failure is addressable: while prompting interventions fail, targeted training that supervises models' internal strategy representations toward state-conditional human preferences narrows the user acceptability generalization gap by a third on out-of-distribution personas and conversational styles.

title: HippocamFLEX: FPGA Prototyping of Hippocampus-Inspired Architecture for Context-Aware Sequence Prediction
authors: Bhuvanesh S. Kayarabettu, Hamed Poursiami, Keiland Cooper, Babak Shahbaba, Norbert Fortin, Maryam Parsa, Akhilesh Jaiswal
abstract: Unlike conventional architectures that treat memory as static pattern storage, the hippocampus organizes experience as ordered sequences and retrieves them through temporally compressed replay spanning prior, current, and anticipated states. This capacity of context-appropriate sequence prediction remains absent from conventional deep learning accelerators and existing neuromorphic fabrics. We present HippocamFLEX, a fully synthesizable digital implementation of these hippocampal computational principles, realized with SystemVerilog RTL on the AMD Zynq UltraScale+,XCZU9EG. The design maps the hippocampal trisynaptic pathway onto three pipeline stages: a Dentate Gyrus / Entorhinal Cortex (DG/EC) stage for hypervector proximity matching, a CA3 stage for context-gated recurrent sequence prediction with multi-phase temporal tagging, and a CA1 stage that integrates past, present, and predicted future events into a theta-sequence inspired output. While much brain-inspired hardware relies on analog mixed-signal design for energy efficiency, this work targets FPGA prototyping as a deliberate architectural choice: FPGAs offer rapid design-space exploration without tape-out cost, bit-exact determinism that simplifies verification. The design supports 64 events across 16 contexts and is verified on physical silicon across context-isolation, temporal-ordering, and mid-sequence sliding-window test cases and is inherently scalable to larger event and context sets.

title: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding and Building "Any-task inference" Capable Foundation Models
authors: Matthew McDermott, Florent Pollet, Payal Chandak, Gregory Kondas, Liat Friedman Antwarg, Noa Dagan, Isaac Kohane
abstract: In this work, we provide a formal framework and mathematical definition for the subset of foundation models focused on enabling the property of "any-task inference" (ATI) (similar to zero-shot inference), rather than those designed for pre-training fine-tuning. To achieve this mathematical definition, we formalize the notion of a "space of tasks of interest," which we include in the problem domain, then provide an interface-based formal definition for ATI foundation models as those that map samples of data $x$ and tasks $t$ to predictions over the space of labels directly. While simple, this definition allows us to show that all ATI foundation models can be decomposed through a "universal task reduction" lens into encoder, model, and decoder aspects. We can leverage this decomposition to also decompose foundation model error into terms corresponding to different aspects of this reduction, stratified into a collection of "design terms," which are theoretical properties that can inform one of whether a particular proposed ATI foundation model can achieve optimality or not due to the structure of the proposed task reduction, and "realized model excess" terms which capture interactions between learned and programmatic components of foundation model systems. Lastly, we can use this perspective to offer two "prototypical" recipes for realizing ATI foundation models in diverse domains, which we term generative and discriminative variants of ATI foundation models. This exercise is grounded throughout by 5 real-world examples of foundation models in different settings, varying greatly in how these capabilities are realized, showing the applicability of this definition to real-world settings.

title: Let LiDAR Decide Where to Look: Geometry-Measured Token Selection for Efficient Sparse Latent World Models
authors: Zeping Zhang, Zhuoya Zhao, Robert Laganière
abstract: Vision-centric autonomous driving models encode thousands of image tokens per frame, yet most depict sky, buildings, or empty road---content irrelevant to planning. Worse, these tokens dilute the planner's attention: we show that randomly discarding 75% of tokens already outperforms the dense model, because the planner can concentrate on the remaining driving-critical content. Building on this finding, we present Geometry-Aware Token Selection (GATS), which uses LiDAR and radar point projections to select a small fraction of image tokens before the vision backbone runs. Because the selector operates on measured 3D geometry rather than visual features, the backbone encodes only the selected patches, cutting end-to-end FLOPs by up to $18\times$. Each kept token receives a 3D anchor from its LiDAR point and is fed to a self-supervised latent world model that predicts future features and 3D displacements without box annotations. At 25% budget, GATS achieves a 3-sec L2 displacement error of 0.520 m on nuScenes and an EPDMS of 88.9 on NAVSIM---surpassing the dense baseline (0.573 m / 85.9) at $6.6\times$ fewer total FLOPs. At an extreme 10% budget (24 GFLOPs, $18\times$ reduction), it still beats the dense baseline on both nuScenes (0.537 m vs. 0.573 m L2) and NAVSIM (87.9 vs. 85.9 EPDMS). On 739 intent-critical scenarios, GATS covers 95.8% of hazardous vehicles and achieves a 0.09% collision rate---73.5% lower than the dense model (0.34%).

title: Fair Recommender Systems for Intersecting Groups
authors: Christine Ling, Juba Ziani
abstract: Recommendation systems that optimize for the average user can fail to capture the preferences of diverse demographic groups. We consider a dynamic recommendation system, where arriving users can belong to different demographic groups. Importantly, these groups can intersect, and a user may belong to several groups. We first show that over time, any group-blind policy (which excludes all current-user group information) recommending $K \geq 1$ items incurs linear total regret under mild conditions. In turn, we introduce three group-aware algorithms based on the classical Upper Confidence Bound algorithm (UCB): i) Intersection-Fitting, which runs UCB on each intersection, but has a sublinear group- and intersection-level regret guarantee with an exponential dependence in the number of groups; and ii) two group-level heuristics, Inner-Outer UCB and Group-Item UCB which allocate different arms to different groups, and use a sleeping expert meta-learner to choose which active group's recommendation an intersection should inherit at any given time step. We provide experimental results on two datasets, Goodreads and BoardGameGeek, and highlight that our heuristics can be preferable to the intersection-fitting algorithm when intersection-level preferences are closely related to group-level preferences, but that intersection-fitting performs better when different intersections within a same group prefer different items.

title: DiRAFT: Privacy-Aware Financial Transcript Synthesis from Aggregate Discourse Priors
authors: Yunbai Zhang, Yunyi Gao, Han-Tai Shiao
abstract: Using customer conversations to train and evaluate financial language models raises confidentiality concerns because non-public financial facts can remain after direct identifiers are masked. Synthetic transcripts offer an alternative data source, but their discourse fidelity and residual confidentiality risks require assessment. We introduce DiRAFT (Discourse Realization from Aggregate First-order Transitions), which extracts financial concept graphs and records the order in which concepts are first introduced. It pools adjacent concept transitions across training records and samples new graph plans from aggregate transition, starting-concept, and plan-length priors. A discourse layer guides text realization without supplying an individual source passage or graph. We assess privacy-related risks through two complementary evaluations: corpus-level structural overlap and source-grounded checks for specific non-public investor facts. The structural assessment covers two financial corpora and three generation backends. The confidential-fact assessment uses human review of 1,400 investor-call outputs across seven strategies and two backends. We also evaluate transition fidelity, content recoverability, and trajectory diversity. Stochastic sampling provides a favorable balance between transition fidelity and structural overlap, with consistent advantages over greedy and top-3 on investor calls. The confidential-fact assessment likewise detects fewer matches for stochastic sampling than these alternatives on both backends covered by the fact assessment. These complementary assessments provide empirical evidence on residual confidentiality risks without establishing a formal guarantee.
comment: 21 pages. Accepted at the Financial AI Security, Privacy and Safety Workshop at ICAIF 2026 (non-archival)

title: The First Few Tokens Matter: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Controllability
authors: Hugh Van Deventer, Dmitrii Troitskii, Laura Ruis
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising way to oversee increasingly capable agents. It succeeds in part because current models appear limited in their ability to control what they verbalize in their reasoning traces. We investigate the source of this limitation and link it to an entropy collapse in the first few tokens following the opening thinking tag. We exploit this mechanism to recover CoT controllability through two inference-time interventions on initial tokens: prefilling, where even a single token can substantially increase controllability, and banning frequent opening tokens combined with in-context examples, which improves average compliance by 34-41 percentage points across models. These interventions recover mainly addition and style controllability (adding or transforming information), while suppression controllability (avoiding or removing information) exhibits more varied responses, suggesting distinct underlying mechanisms. Consistent with this, the two groups behave as separate capabilities: across models, performance correlates positively within these groups, while cross-group correlations are mostly negative. Importantly, we find that the relationship with monitorability depends on the evaluation: addition and style controllability more consistently positively correlate with monitorability, while suppression often shows negative associations. Our findings motivate the development of controllability evaluations that distinguish difficulty initiating a specific opening from general limitations of the ability to alter reasoning content, alongside separate reporting of control tasks and categories.

title: Benchmarking Forecasting Agents on Yesterday's Tomorrows
authors: Yuxuan Wang, Yishu Wang, Jiaqi Deng
abstract: Digital agents can now gather and organize information, reason over it, and use tools to complete complex tasks. Forecasting puts all of these abilities to the test: it requires integrating incomplete evidence, inferring causal drivers, and committing to calibrated probabilistic judgments. Existing benchmarks are poorly suited to measuring and improving this ability. Live benchmarks provide feedback only after events resolve, so every evaluation cycle waits on the calendar; fixed-corpus evaluations return results immediately but confine research to pre-collected documents. We introduce FABench, a scalable backtesting environment for Forecasting Agents. An automated pipeline discovers events, generates questions, and resolves outcomes for any past forecast date, so the benchmark can be renewed to stay ahead of model training cutoffs; its first release poses 287 questions across nine domains. Agents research each question freely in an archive environment that combines an offline archive with live web search screened to prevent temporal leakage. Evaluating agents built on eight recent models, we find that retrieval improves the Brier score of all eight in every retrieval setting and lifts the leading agents to the market consensus on the 54 questions linked to Polymarket, with the best three scoring slightly above it. Research traces reveal recurring failures in how agents weigh and apply evidence, leaving ample room for improvement. We release our code, data, and archive environment as a foundation for community research on forecasting agents.

title: Integrating of Attack Patterns and Threat Modeling to Support Security Analysis in the Automotive Domain
authors: Eduardo Santos de Oliveira Marques, Saulo Moraes Villela, Heder Soares Bernardino, Alex Borges Vieira, Bernardo Martins Rocha, André Luiz de Oliveira
abstract: The increasing connectivity of cyber-physical systems in the automotive domain demands systematic approaches for identifying and mitigating cybersecurity threats. While ISO 21434 defines a structured workflow for Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA), it does not prescribe a specific method for identifying attack paths or evaluating risks. This paper proposes a conceptual model grounded in ISO 21434 that integrates the STRIDE threat classification with the CAPEC attack pattern database, focusing on the identification of attack scenarios and risk assessment. Its applicability is demonstrated through a case study involving Bluetooth-based threats to an automotive headlamp system.

title: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms
authors: Michel Fabrice Serret, Laura Grigori
abstract: The bottleneck of attention mechanisms, which are the fundamental building block of modern language models, is their quadratic complexity in terms of context size. There has thus been an increasing interest in the compression of the context, also called KV-cache compression. In this article, we consider the problem of compressing the context of attention mechanisms by first formulating it in the Hilbert space associated with its kernel. In this formalism, attention can be represented as the ratio of two linear maps whose interpolant is also the ratio of interpolants, this allows us to consider the interpolation of the linear maps directly. We thus introduce two novel KV-cache compression methods which we call GAIM and Q-DAIM, based on the Generalized Empirical Interpolation Method (GEIM) and the Q-Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method (Q-DEIM), respectively. As the cost of these methods is quadratic in terms of context length, we propose surrogate models based on the Taylor series, the Performer and the Random Fourier Features method which allow the compression to be done in linear time. Finally, we extend this result to the streaming attention setting, providing new methods which allow one to penalize the selection of interpolation nodes based on the previously interpolated context and to update the previous interpolation based on new information. We then provide numerical results on the convergence of the residuals and the output error in future queries and preliminary results on the LongBench-E benchmark showing performance comparable to the state-of-the-art methods. These experiments suggest that the range revealed by our Q-DAIM method could help identify where information is concentrated in the KV cache, thus enabling an efficient compression.

title: Opening the Box Changes the Cat: LLMs Detect Chain-of-Thought Monitoring - What now?
authors: Amir Jalilifard, Marcos Medeiros Raimundo, Anderson Rocha
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning allows large language models (LLMs) to generate intermediate reasoning traces in natural language while solving complex tasks. These traces can support safety monitoring by exposing potentially harmful plans before actions are executed. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which LLMs infer the presence of CoT monitoring from direct and indirect environmental cues and examine how this inference affects their subsequent behavior. Our observations suggest that oversight is an interactive process: while a monitor inspects a model's reasoning, traces left by monitoring interventions can allow the model to infer that its thoughts are being observed and to adapt its behavior accordingly. We show that even subtle environmental cues, such as timing-related signals from timeouts and operation durations, can reveal the presence of monitoring and trigger models to adapt their behavior. Across repeated episodes and interaction loops, we further observe that models can form statistical estimates of the monitor's effectiveness and use these estimates to guide attempts to evade detection. These findings highlight the need to evaluate CoT-based oversight under adaptive conditions, where the monitoring process itself may influence the behavior it seeks to observe.

title: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yu Li, Yufa Zhou, Tian Lan
abstract: On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models assumes that training responses are sampled from the current policy. In practice, an inference engine samples the responses and a separate trainer computes the gradients, and the \textbf{training-inference mismatch} between the two makes the training data off-policy. The mismatch has two sources, the numerics of the engine and the stale weights of asynchronous sampling, and a correction that stabilizes training under one source can fail under the other. \textit{We ask which property of a mismatch source decides the correction it needs.} Evaluating the trainer at the sampler's weights splits each sampled-token error exactly into a \textit{numerical discrepancy} of the engine and a \textit{policy lag} of the trainer, and we follow both through training. The numerical discrepancy stays approximately constant, so it biases the updates by a nearly fixed amount, and centering the score at each prefix removes its leading bias. The policy lag is produced by the trainer's own updates: the bias it leaves enters the next update, which enlarges the next lag and closes a feedback loop. Importance weighting cuts this loop only while the lag ratio stays concentrated, and on Qwen3-1.7B it fails at the step where the effective sample size of the ratio falls below one half. From this account we derive the \textbf{discrepancy-lag correction} (DLC), which centers the numerical discrepancy, clips the lag ratio against the sampler's weights and resynchronizes the sampler when this effective sample size falls below one half. Under a stale sampler, DLC keeps the KL divergence from on-policy training within twice the KL between two independent on-policy trainings on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, and its resynchronization prevents collapses that the per-token corrections leave and that a KL measured on the sampler's prefixes does not detect.

title: UFMF: Radar-Guided Kinematic Priors for Real-Time 4D Occupancy Forecasting
authors: Zeping Zhang, Zhuoya Zhao, Robert Laganière
abstract: Real-time 4D occupancy forecasting requires reliably extrapolating both ego motion and surrounding actor motion under strict latency budgets. Recent occupancy world models improve long-horizon fidelity through generative decoders and 3D volumetric modeling, yet their computational cost makes real-time deployment challenging. Light-weight BEV forecasters meet latency requirements but often blur or suppress fast-moving actors at longer horizons. We present UFMF (Ultra-Fast Multi-modal Forecaster), a real-time forecaster that keeps an attention-free diagonal state-space temporal core while injecting targeted kinematic and geometric structure where lightweight models typically fail. A radar-guided velocity-aware dynamic prior (VADP) decomposes future displacement into a linear extrapolation plus a learned horizon-dependent residual. The resulting per-cell flow fields transport a compact dynamic latent subspace during rollout. Two auxiliary training constraints complement this branch: world-frame dynamic supervision enforces inter-horizon trajectory coherence, and class-conditioned vertical-profile supervision regularizes BEV-to-3D lifting. UFMF operates at 122 FPS on a single RTX 4090 and reaches 0.45 fast-displacement mIoU on nuScenes, outperforming recent occupancy world models at a fraction of their computational cost.

title: CAMEL: Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning for Ultra-Lightweight Retinal Foundation Models
authors: Andre Guarnier De Mitri, Giovani Decico Lucafo, Miller Matheus Lima Anacleto Rocha, Diego Furtado Silva
abstract: Recent progress in deep learning has substantially advanced automated grading of ophthalmologic pathologies, supported by large annotated datasets and improved representation learning. However, a significant gap remains between state-of-the-art performance and clinical scalability. In particular, foundation models have reshaped image-based medical screening and diagnosis. These large-scale architectures trained on extensive datasets learn rich, generalizable feature representations that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. In ophthalmology, RETFound, one of the most relevant foundation models for retinal images, performs strongly across classification, segmentation, and risk prediction tasks. Despite their effectiveness, foundation models are often computationally prohibitive, hindering their deployment in real-world clinical environments where hardware constraints and latency are critical. To bridge this gap, we introduce CAMEL (Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning), a novel cross-architecture distillation framework that uses an asymmetric masking strategy during embedding learning to effectively transfer knowledge from massive teacher foundation models to compact, lightweight student models. Our experimental evaluation across four datasets shows that CAMEL preserves accuracy while drastically reducing computational complexity, enabling lightweight yet highly accurate models suitable for resource-limited clinical settings.

title: AVID: A Weakly Aligned RGB-Infrared Dataset and Perturbation Benchmark for Tiny Aerial Targets
authors: Dharini Raghavan, Vishnu Rao, Sethu Selvi S
abstract: Long-range detection of small drones is complicated by their visual similarity to birds and by the limited detail available from ground-based cameras. Combining visible and infrared observations offers complementary information, but their usefulness depends on target size, cross-modal alignment, and image quality. We present AVID, a benchmark for studying these factors using real RGB-infrared bird-drone surveillance footage originating from the Drone Detection Dataset and curated for the IEEE ICIP 2025 Video and Image Processing Cup. AVID comprises 32,040 corresponding frame pairs from 115 videos, with 35,952 existing bird and drone annotations at $320\times256$ resolution. Targets occupy an unusually narrow size range: 68.1\% have a geometric-mean bounding-box side of 8--16 pixels, and 99.0\% meet the COCO small-object criterion. To characterize the geometric difficulty of combining the modalities, we introduce an object-relative alignment ratio and an alignment burden curve. In a sample of 300 frame pairs, 32.3\% have estimated global translations greater than 5 pixels; among the 264 pairs with matching annotations, 16.3\% exceed one median target side. We further introduce AVID-C, which simulates seven families of image degradation at five severity levels independently in RGB, infrared, or both. A fixed-feature analysis examines how scale, degradation, and added cross-modal shifts affect fitted bird-drone class overlap. At 12--16 pixels, the Bhattacharyya error bounds are 0.148 for RGB, 0.198 for infrared, and 0.046 for their combined features. These values describe separation in the specified feature and density models, not detector accuracy. Together, AVID and AVID-C support scale-aware, alignment-aware, and sensor-specific studies of tiny aerial targets.

title: A Mixed $H_{\infty}$--Passivity Approach for Leveraging Heat-Pump-Connected District Heating Systems as Frequency Support in Electric Power Systems
authors: Xinyi Yi, Ioannis Lestas
abstract: Heat-pump (HP)-connected district heating systems (DHSs) can support grid frequency by rapidly modulating HP electrical consumption while accommodating the resulting heat imbalance. Thermal-state-informed HP control improves EPS--DHS coordination, but introduces slower DHS dynamics and heat-side disturbance propagation at the electrical interface on the time scale of secondary frequency control. This paper formulates the regulated DHS as a grid-facing dynamic port and develops a mixed $H_\infty$--passivity framework for disturbance-independent temperature regulation while preserving a clean electrical response during secondary frequency control. Sufficient conditions guarantee local asymptotic stability of the EPS--HP--DHS interconnection across primary frequency control, secondary frequency control, and DHS regulation. These stability conditions are integrated with multi-channel $H_\infty$ attenuation of DHS-state-dependent electrical dynamics, heat-disturbance propagation, and DHS-regulation errors, yielding a tractable convex LMI program for controller synthesis. Cross-model validation deploys controllers synthesized on control-oriented EPS--DHS models, without retuning, on an open-source electromechanical IEEE 39-bus model coupled with four high-fidelity finite-volume DHS models retaining thermal transport, storage, and heat-loss dynamics. The resulting controller improves EPS--DHS coordination without compromising the grid-facing electrical response.

title: Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel
authors: Arslan Iamaletdinov, Elfat Sabitov, Konstantin Sorokin
abstract: We introduce the Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel (MCRWK), an estimator whose per-pair cost is independent of graph size and derived directly from the random walk kernel (RWK) expansion. By normalizing the kernel coefficients, MCRWK samples a shared walk length and estimates its contribution using random walks on the input graphs. This gives a simple way to approximate RWK without constructing the product graph. For a fixed expected walk length and efficient neighbor sampling, each pairwise estimate takes $O(m)$ time for $m$ Monte Carlo samples, allowing the sample budget to control the trade-off between runtime and accuracy. We evaluate MCRWK against Graph Voyagers and classical RWK methods on synthetic and real graph datasets. In the reported experiments on large synthetic graphs, MCRWK is faster than Graph Voyagers and, at matched runtime, more accurate. It also has the lowest Gram-matrix runtime on the five real datasets studied. Code and experiments are available at https://github.com/arslan-yam/random_walk_kernels_computations

title: Renegotiable Options Fail to Prevent Hold-Up Between Two Profit-Maximizing Frontier LLM Agents
authors: Junwei Yao, Zike Yang, Yongxi Zhou, Yanxian Chen, Jianan Liu, Jiaxi Wen, Zhijun Wang
abstract: Do contract terms that protect investment between people also protect it between profit-maximizing language-model agents? In the hold-up problem, a seller can adapt a unit to one buyer at a cost before the price is set. Once that cost is sunk, the buyer can offer almost nothing and the seller will still accept, so a seller who foresees this does not adapt. One remedy is an option: the buyer may buy at a fixed price. In theory the option stops working if the buyer can let it lapse and offer its own price instead. Yet in a laboratory experiment by Hoppe and Schmitz, this renegotiable option raised human investment from 41.5% of pairs without a contract to 67.2%. We had Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, each told to maximize its side's profit, play a one-shot game with the same strategic structure under their four contract regimes and a reference-price control. The agents did what game theory predicts: under the renegotiable option no seller adapted, and under the option that rules out this renegotiation every seller did. In a second experiment in which sellers no longer stated their expected revenue before deciding, removing the profit instruction left investment unchanged under no contract and both options. When we changed the numbers so that the buyer would exercise the option even without adaptation, adapting only added cost, and no seller adapted: the agents did not simply adapt whenever an option was offered or whenever its price covered the cost. Under our protocol, a contract term that raised investment between people did not protect it between agents.

title: Better Retrievers, Worse Labels: How Incomplete Relevance Judgments Distort Abstention Evaluation in Conversational RAG
authors: Ivan Kochergin, Vasily Konovalov
abstract: Conversational RAG benchmarks such as MTRAG and RETECO evaluate retrieval and generation end to end: each system answers from its own retrieval, so abstention must be scored against whether each retrieved context is sufficient. A convenient shortcut reads sufficiency off the relevance judgments and treats a context without gold documents as unanswerable. We re-run the official baselines exactly and test this shortcut on RECOR (RETECO track~2) with four retrievers (nDCG@10 from .18 to .59) and three Qwen3 readers. Two open LLM judges and a panel of four small open models label each context by content, and a model of another family audits 250 contexts blind, with adjudication. The stronger the retriever, the larger the share of no-gold contexts that still contain the answer (28\% to 72\%) and the lower the shortcut's precision (.68 to .10; .70 to .21 under the audit). A reader agrees: Qwen3-4B answers 62--67\% of these false misses correctly, against 23--30\% of no-gold contexts judged insufficient and 1\% with no documents. In most false misses, the answer comes from a hard negative mined for the same question, another turn's gold or a neighbouring chunk of the gold page. On MTRAG, whose judgments come from annotators, precision drops from .72 to .50. Under the shortcut, answerability AUROC is up to .19 too low, and the best sufficiency detector appears to be a retrieval score that never reads the documents. We release code, runs and labels, and recommend scoring refusals against content labels, not the presence of gold.

title: Nedimo: An Evidence-Grounded Multilingual Pipeline for AI-Generated Sleep Stories
authors: Georgios Makridis, Stefanos Kampouris
abstract: Generative audio systems can produce large libraries of personalized bedtime content, but ordinary media objectives (retention, completion, and novelty) are poorly aligned with the goal of supporting a transition toward sleep. Direct evidence for narrated bedtime audio in adults is mixed, and a recent active-controlled trial did not support such audio as a standalone treatment for sleep disturbance.
